subject: Acceptance window flattening and risk elevations
messages:
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <ep@novahealth.ai>, Procurement <procurement@novahealth.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acceptance window flattening — proposed risk mitigations

Hi Elena / NovaHealth procurement team,

Thanks for the call this morning. Based on what we heard from your engineering and security leads, the evaluation gating has less tolerance for staggered acceptance windows. To keep the overall go-live in Q3 while reducing risk, we propose a short “flattening” of the MAP: compress the last two acceptance milestones into a single 5-day window with a guarded rollback lane and a pre-approved remediation credit.

Attached: MAP_v1.xlsx (current MAP annotated with the proposed compression).

Key asks from your side so we can finalize:
- Confirm a 5-day consolidated acceptance window is feasible for your QA team
- Confirm who is the executive approver for the remediation credit (name + email)
- Confirm procurement constraints on invoicing dates if go-live shifts by up to 14 days

We think this approach keeps your QA visibility while reducing the number of context switches on our side. If this is acceptable we will produce a short rebaseline proposal and an escalation ladder (exec contact + credit thresholds) and share it with procurement by end of day.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Elena Park <ep@novahealth.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@novahealth.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance window flattening — proposed risk mitigations

Laura —

Appreciate the summary and the worksheet. Quick notes from our side after huddling with QA and Security:
- QA can accommodate a 5-day consolidated window but we will need a fixed, instrumented test plan (test-run checklist + pass/fail gates) at least 48 hours before the window starts.
- Security is concerned about the rollback lane: we need a documented rollback plan and confirmation that any hotfixes will be sandbox-tested for 24 hours before production revert.
- Procurement: we cannot move invoice dates arbitrarily; any change that impacts billing needs prior notice and a signed MPA amendment.

Procurement copied Procurement (procurement@novahealth.ai) to flag the billing constraint.

I can get you the exec approver for remediation credit (David Singh) — he’s looped on this thread.

On timing: we might need up to 14 calendar days to rework our internal test schedule, so please include a conservative cost delta in the proposal.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Director, Product Ops | NovaHealth AI

Subject: Rebaseline proposal + escalation ladder (draft)

Elena / David / procurement —

Thanks for the quick feedback. Attached is a short rebaseline proposal (rebaseline_proposal.pdf) and a cost impact CSV (cost_impact_delta.csv) showing estimated unit cost of a 0 / 7 / 14 day slide. High-level summary below:

Proposal (recommended):
- Consolidate final acceptance milestones into a single 5-day window
- Start: target week-of Jul 5 (flexible within 2 weeks)
- Escalation ladder: two exec contacts (David Singh, VP Product) and Laura Bennett (Redwood AE) for day-zero escalations; Rishi M. to handle technical rollback coordination.
- Pre-approved remediation credit: up to 5% of the first-month invoice if a post-cutover rollback is required due to Redwood deliverables. Financial terms to be captured in an MPA amendment.
- Required deliverables from NovaHealth: instrumented test plan and sign-off owner 48 hours prior to window

Risk notes:
- If NovaHealth needs >14 days slide, Redwood will need to re-evaluate dedicated capacity reservations for the reserved GPU pool (lead time impacts may change pricing).
- If rollback testing takes longer than 24 hours beyond the planned window, we will trigger the escalation ladder and may apply the remediation credit mechanism.

Next steps:
1) David / Procurement: confirm approval for the remediation credit authority and who will sign the amendment
2) NovaHealth QA: share instrumented test plan by Jun 25
3) Redwood (Rishi / Camila): produce final MAP_v2 (with gating checklist) by Jun 18

If that timeline works I will coordinate a short exec alignment call for Monday.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: rebaseline_proposal.pdf, cost_impact_delta.csv
From: David Singh <d.singh@novahealth.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <ep@novahealth.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@novahealth.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 14:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rebaseline proposal + escalation ladder (draft)

Laura / Elena —

Thank you for the clear proposal. I'm comfortable with the 5-day consolidated acceptance window and the escalation ladder as written. Procurement: please confirm the MPA amendment language for a pre-approved remediation credit up to 5% and whether we can sign an amendment that preserves the current invoice date while acknowledging a potential 14-day operational slide.

Two asks from our side before exec alignment:
- Please quantify the expected cost delta for a 14-day slide versus no slide (the CSV helps but we need a short paragraph summarizing impact to committed vs. flexible capacity).
- Confirm Redwood’s rollback testing checklist and where logs will be stored for audit (we need traceable rollback evidence for our SOC process).

If both are OK, happy to join the Monday alignment call.

-David
